ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠂ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ ᠢ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ
ᠬᠣᠣᠰ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ ᠂ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠂
ᠰᠡᠳᱠᠢᠯ ᠦᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠂ ᠦᠨᠡᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠲᠤ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ

<warning>Red woodblock print is faded and low-contrast against the paper in several columns; column 16 contains an unprinted blank interval in the middle of the line.</warning>
<margin><term>Niγuča</term> <gloss>Secret Scripture</gloss>, First Volume, two hundred and eighty, upper <note>recto folio marker in Mongolian: "ᠨᠢᠭᠤᠴᠠ ᠲᠡᠷᠢᠭᠦᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠨᠠᠶᠠᠨ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ"</note></margin>
<margin>Secret Scripture, First Fascicle, upper part, folio two hundred and eighty <note>original Chinese marginal signature: "秘密經第一卷上二百八十"</note></margin>
to transform into, and of the mind that establishes the <term>sedkil-ün činar</term> <gloss>nature of mind</gloss>,
the <term>tegünčilen iregsen</term> <gloss>Thus-Come One, Sanskrit Tathāgata</gloss>, who has revealed the <term>nom-un činar</term> <gloss>true nature of phenomena, Sanskrit dharmatā</gloss> of all things:
having become the nature of goodness and abiding therein, the nature of all phenomena
is well-established, and is the <term>belge bilig</term> <gloss>primordial wisdom, Sanskrit jñāna</gloss> of the Thus-Come One.
Having attained the nature of mind, within the nature of all Buddhas,
the supreme primordial wisdom, the essential mind of all Thus-Come Ones,
the <term>ilaju tegüs nögčigsen</term> <gloss>Victoriously Transcended One, Sanskrit Bhagavān</gloss>, is the nature of all phenomena.
Without inherent nature <note>devoid of independent self-existence, Sanskrit svabhāva</note>, having established and revealed the nature of mind:
the Victoriously Transcended One, who has attained the nature of the Thus-Come One,
the nature of phenomena, abiding in the primordial wisdom of all Buddhas,
the All-Knowing One, who has revealed the nature of mind:
thus it is declared, and it is the nature of all Thus-Come Ones.
Made manifest and revealed, it is the realization of the nature of mind.
The all-perfect nature, having become the nature of primordial wisdom,
transcendently victorious, is called the nature of all phenomena.
The All-Knowing One, <note>unprinted blank interval in the woodblock between two punctuation marks</note> within the nature of mind,
having established the six natures <note>the six elements or six sense-bases in Buddhist tantric cosmology</note> and the primordial wisdom of all Buddhas,
non-dual primordial wisdom, which has revealed the nature of all phenomena,
the nature of mind, abides in the true nature <note>ultimate reality, Sanskrit bhūtakoṭi</note>.
So it is, for it has revealed the <term>niγuča</term> <gloss>secret</gloss> nature of all Thus-Come Ones.
Having become manifest, and abiding in the primordial wisdom of all Buddhas,
the nature of this is the nature of all phenomena.
The Victoriously Transcended One, in whom the nature of all Thus-Come Ones abides,
having thoroughly attained the true nature, is the nature of primordial wisdom,

<summary>This folio from the first volume of the Mongolian Kanjur tantra section, identified in the bilingual Mongolian and Chinese marginalia as the Secret Scripture, expounds the identity between the nature of mind, the true nature of all phenomena, and the non-dual primordial wisdom of all Buddhas and Thus-Come Ones.</summary>
<keywords>Secret Scripture, Guhyasamaja, Mongolian Kanjur, nature of mind, dharmata, primordial wisdom, Tathagata, Bhagavan, non-dual wisdom, Esoteric Buddhism</keywords>
